questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Using average bond enthalpies N≡N 945 kJ/mol, H–H 436 kJ/mol and N–H 391 kJ/mol, how much heat is released when 0.50 mol of $\text{N}_2(g)$ reacts completely with excess $\text{H}_2(g)$ to form $\text{NH}_3(g)$?
questions.explanation: Bonds broken are one N≡N and three H–H, totalling $945+3(436)=2253$ kJ per mole of $\text{N}_2$. Bonds formed are six N–H, totalling $6(391)=2346$ kJ. The change is $-93$ kJ per mole of $\text{N}_2$, so 0.50 mol releases $46.5$ kJ. Forgetting to scale by 0.50 mol gives 93 kJ, scaling by a quarter gives 23.3 kJ, and doubling gives 186 kJ.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The sulphate ion $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ is drawn with two S=O double bonds and two S–O$^-$ single bonds. What is the sum of the absolute values of all formal charges in this drawing?
questions.explanation: Sulphur has four bonds and no lone pair, so $FC_S=6-0-6=0$. Both double-bonded oxygens have $FC=0$. Each of the two singly bonded oxygens has three lone pairs and one bond, so $FC=6-6-1=-1$. The absolute sum is $0+0+0+1+1=2$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: How many lone pairs does the central xenon atom carry in the molecule $\text{XeF}_2$?
questions.explanation: Xenon and two fluorines supply $8+14=22$ electrons, which is 11 pairs. The two Xe–F bonds use 2 pairs and each fluorine keeps 3 lone pairs (6 pairs), leaving $11-2-6=3$ pairs on xenon.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Two bond dipoles of 1.5 D each act in a molecule at a bond angle of 120°. What is the magnitude of their resultant dipole moment?
questions.explanation: For two vectors of equal magnitude $\mu$ at angle $\theta$, the resultant is $R=\sqrt{2\mu^2(1+\cos\theta)}$. With $\cos 120^\circ=-0.5$, this gives $R=\sqrt{2(2.25)(0.5)}=1.5$ D, the same as one bond dipole. Using 60° instead gives 2.6 D, adding the magnitudes gives 3.0 D, and perfect cancellation gives 0 D.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: What is the difference between the number of electrons in bonding molecular levels and the number in antibonding molecular levels of the cation $\text{F}_2^+$?
questions.explanation: $\text{F}_2^+$ has 17 electrons. Ten occupy bonding levels and seven occupy antibonding levels. The difference is $10-7=3$, which equals twice the bond order of 1.5. Reading the total electron count of 17 as the answer would be the error to avoid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The cyanide ion $\text{CN}^-$ is drawn with a triple bond between C and N, one lone pair on nitrogen and one lone pair on carbon. What is the formal charge on nitrogen minus the formal charge on carbon in this drawing?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen has $FC=5-2-3=0$ and carbon has $FC=4-2-3=-1$ in this drawing. Their difference is $0-(-1)=+1$. Subtracting in the other order gives −1, while treating both atoms as neutral gives 0, and doubling the carbon charge gives +2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: How many lone pairs in total are present over all atoms of the molecule $\text{ClF}_3$, which has three Cl–F single bonds?
questions.explanation: Chlorine and three fluorines supply $7+21=28$ electrons, or 14 pairs. The three Cl–F bonds use 3 pairs, which leaves 11 pairs as lone pairs: 9 on the fluorines and 2 on chlorine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: What is the sum of the bond orders of the species $\text{He}_2^+$ and $\text{H}_2^+$?
questions.explanation: $\text{He}_2^+$ has 3 electrons, two in a bonding level and one in an antibonding level, so $BO=(2-1)/2=0.5$. $\text{H}_2^+$ has a single bonding electron, so its bond order is also 0.5. The sum is $0.5+0.5=1.0$. Giving $\text{He}_2^+$ a bond order of 1 produces 1.5, and taking both as 1 produces 2.0.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The carbon in methane forms sp3 hybrid orbitals, while carbon in ethene forms sp2 hybrid orbitals for its C–H bonds. What is the ratio of the percentage s-character of an sp2 orbital to that of an sp3 orbital?
questions.explanation: An sp2 hybrid has one-third s-character, about 33.3%, and an sp3 hybrid has one-quarter, or 25%. The ratio is $33.3/25\approx 1.33$. The inverse gives 0.75, and 1.50 comes from using sp hybrids at 50% in the numerator. Taking 33.3/50 gives 0.67.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: What is the total number of sigma bonds in one molecule of propyne, $\text{CH}_3\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$?
questions.explanation: Propyne has four C–H sigma bonds and two C–C sigma bonds, one for the single bond and one within the triple bond. The two pi bonds of the triple bond are not sigma bonds. The total is $4+2=6$. Counting the pi bonds as well would give 8.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: What is the ratio of the bond order of $\text{N}_2$ to the bond order of $\text{O}_2$?
questions.explanation: $\text{N}_2$ has a bond order of 3 and $\text{O}_2$ has a bond order of 2, so the ratio is $3/2=1.50$. Inverting gives 0.67, and using 4 as the bond order of $\text{N}_2$ gives 2.00. Treating both bond orders as equal gives 1.00.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The phosphate ion $\text{PO}_4^{3-}$ is drawn with four P–O single bonds. What is the formal charge on phosphorus in this drawing?
questions.explanation: Phosphorus has 5 valence electrons, no lone pair and four bonding electrons from its four single bonds, so $FC=5-0-4=+1$. Using 5 as the formal charge gives +5, and using the net ion charge of −3 gives −3. Assigning the oxygen charges to phosphorus gives +3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: What is the total number of valence electrons in the nitrite ion $\text{NO}_2^-$?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen contributes 5 valence electrons and the two oxygens contribute $2\times 6=12$, giving 17. The extra electron from the 1− charge brings the total to 18. Forgetting the charge gives 17.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Given an average C–H bond enthalpy of 413 kJ/mol, how many kJ are required to break all the C–H bonds in 0.25 mol of methane, $\text{CH}_4$?
questions.explanation: Each $\text{CH}_4$ molecule has four C–H bonds, so 0.25 mol of methane contains $0.25\times 4=1.00$ mol of bonds. Multiplying by 413 kJ/mol gives 413 kJ. Counting one bond per molecule gives 103.25 kJ, doubling the bond count gives 826 kJ, and 1652 kJ uses four times the bond count.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The phosphate ion $\text{PO}_4^{3-}$ is drawn with four P–O single bonds and no double bonds. What is the sum of the absolute values of all formal charges in this drawing?
questions.explanation: Phosphorus has $FC=5-0-4=+1$. Each of the four oxygens carries three lone pairs and one bond, so $FC=6-6-1=-1$. The absolute sum is $1+4(1)=5$. The signed sum of −3 equals the net charge and is not what is asked.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: For the xenon compounds $\text{XeF}_2$, $\text{XeF}_4$ and $\text{XeO}_3$, consider these statements: (I) $\text{XeF}_2$ is linear; (II) $\text{XeF}_4$ is square planar; (III) $\text{XeO}_3$ is trigonal pyramidal. Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: $\text{XeF}_2$ has five electron domains with three lone pairs in equatorial positions, giving a linear molecule, so I is true. $\text{XeF}_4$ has six domains with two lone pairs opposite each other, giving a square planar shape, so II is true. $\text{XeO}_3$ has three bonded oxygens and one lone pair on xenon, giving a trigonal pyramidal shape, so III is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: How many lone pairs are on the central chlorine atom in the chlorate ion $\text{ClO}_3^-$, drawn with one Cl=O double bond and two Cl–O$^-$ single bonds?
questions.explanation: Chlorate has $7+18+1=26$ valence electrons, or 13 pairs. The bonds account for 4 pairs, the double-bonded oxygen keeps 2 pairs and the two singly bonded oxygens keep 3 pairs each, a total of 8 pairs. The remaining pair sits on chlorine. Forgetting the extra electron from the charge gives 0 for chlorine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Using average bond enthalpies C–H 413, Cl–Cl 242, C–Cl 328 and H–Cl 431 kJ/mol, what is $\Delta H$ for $\text{CH}_4(g)+\text{Cl}_2(g)\rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{Cl}(g)+\text{HCl}(g)$?
questions.explanation: Only one C–H bond and one Cl–Cl bond are broken, totalling $413+242=655$ kJ. One C–Cl bond and one H–Cl bond are formed, totalling $328+431=759$ kJ. So $\Delta H=655-759=-104$ kJ/mol, which is exothermic. Reversing the sign gives +104, using only the bonds formed gives −759, and using only the bonds broken gives +655.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: For the species $\text{NO}_2^+$, $\text{NO}_2$ and $\text{NO}_2^-$, consider these statements: (I) $\text{NO}_2^+$ is linear; (II) $\text{NO}_2$ has an odd number of electrons; (III) each N–O bond in $\text{NO}_2^-$ has a bond order of 2. Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: $\text{NO}_2^+$ has two N=O bonds and no lone pair on nitrogen, which gives a linear arrangement, so I is true. $\text{NO}_2$ has $5+12=17$ valence electrons, which is odd, so II is true. In $\text{NO}_2^-$ the two N–O bonds are equivalent through resonance and each has bond order 1.5, so III is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In the molecule $\text{O}_2\text{N}\text{–}\text{NO}_2$, each nitrogen forms one N=O double bond and one N–O single bond, and the two nitrogens are joined by one N–N single bond. How many sigma bonds are in the molecule?
questions.explanation: The N–N bond is a sigma bond. Each of the four N–O connections, including the two N=O double bonds, contributes one sigma bond. The pi components of the two N=O bonds are not counted. The total is $1+4=5$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Two identical bond dipoles, each 1.2 D, are separated by an angle of 60° in a molecule. What is the magnitude of their resultant dipole moment, to two decimal places?
questions.explanation: For two vectors of magnitude $\mu$ at angle $\theta$, $R=\sqrt{2\mu^2(1+\cos\theta)}$. With $\cos 60^\circ=0.5$, $R=\sqrt{2(1.44)(1.5)}=\sqrt{4.32}\approx 2.08$ D. Adding the magnitudes gives 2.40 D, ignoring one dipole gives 1.20 D, and cancellation gives 0.00 D.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider $\text{CCl}_4$, $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$ and $\text{CHCl}_3$. Statements: (I) $\text{CCl}_4$ is nonpolar; (II) $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$ is polar; (III) $\text{CHCl}_3$ is nonpolar. Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: $\text{CCl}_4$ is tetrahedral with four identical bonds, so its bond dipoles cancel and I is true. $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$ has two different substituents arranged so that the bond dipoles do not cancel, so II is true. $\text{CHCl}_3$ also has an unequal set of bonds, so its net dipole is nonzero and III is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: What is the total number of valence electrons in one molecule of xenon trioxide, $\text{XeO}_3$?
questions.explanation: Xenon contributes 8 valence electrons and the three oxygens contribute $3\times 6=18$. The total is $8+18=26$. Using the oxygen count of two gives 20, which is the wrong molecule.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Among $\text{O}_2^-$, $\text{O}_2$, $\text{O}_2^+$ and $\text{O}_2^{2-}$, which species has the shortest O–O bond?
questions.explanation: Bond length falls as bond order rises. The bond orders are 1.5 for $\text{O}_2^-$, 2 for $\text{O}_2$, 2.5 for $\text{O}_2^+$ and 1 for $\text{O}_2^{2-}$. The highest value, 2.5, belongs to $\text{O}_2^+$, so it has the shortest bond. Choosing $\text{O}_2^{2-}$ confuses the shortest bond with the lowest bond order.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: How many electrons occupy pi bonds in one molecule of propyne, $\text{CH}_3\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$?
questions.explanation: Propyne contains one carbon–carbon triple bond, which has two pi bonds. Each pi bond holds two electrons, so the total is $2\times 2=4$. Counting only one pi bond for the triple bond gives 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: What is the total number of pi bonds in one molecule of $\text{SO}_3$ drawn with three S=O double bonds, plus the number in one molecule of ethene, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$?
questions.explanation: Each of the three S=O double bonds contains one pi bond, giving 3. Ethene has one C=C double bond with one pi bond. The total is $3+1=4$. Drawing $\text{SO}_3$ with only one double bond would give 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In the square pyramidal molecule $\text{BrF}_5$, how many F–Br–F bond angles are exactly 90°?
questions.explanation: The apical fluorine makes a 90° angle with each of the four basal fluorines, giving 4 angles. Each pair of adjacent basal fluorines also makes a 90° angle, giving 4 more. The opposite basal pairs are 180° apart. The total is $4+4=8$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: For the species $\text{F}_2$, $\text{F}_2^+$ and $\text{F}_2^-$, consider these statements: (I) $\text{F}_2$ is diamagnetic with bond order 1; (II) $\text{F}_2^+$ is diamagnetic; (III) $\text{F}_2^-$ has bond order 0.5. Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: $\text{F}_2$ has 18 electrons, all paired, with $BO=(10-8)/2=1$, so I is true. $\text{F}_2^+$ has 17 electrons and one unpaired electron, so it is paramagnetic and II is false. $\text{F}_2^-$ has 19 electrons, giving $BO=(10-9)/2=0.5$, so III is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: What is the total number of unpaired electrons in one ion of $\text{He}_2^+$ plus one molecule of $\text{B}_2$?
questions.explanation: $\text{He}_2^+$ has 3 electrons, two in a bonding level and one in an antibonding level, leaving one unpaired. $\text{B}_2$ has two unpaired electrons in its degenerate $\pi_{2p}$ levels. The total is $1+2=3$. Treating $\text{B}_2$ as diamagnetic gives 1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Nitric acid, $\text{HNO}_3$, is drawn with one N=O double bond, one N–OH single bond and one N–O$^-$ single bond, with nitrogen carrying no lone pair. What is the sum of the absolute values of all formal charges, including hydrogen?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen has $FC=5-0-4=+1$. The double-bonded oxygen and the hydroxyl oxygen each have $FC=0$, since the hydroxyl oxygen has two lone pairs and two bonds. The singly bonded oxygen carries $FC=-1$, and hydrogen has zero formal charge. The absolute sum is $1+1=2$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Using average bond enthalpies H–H 436 kJ/mol, F–F 158 kJ/mol and H–F 565 kJ/mol, what is $\Delta H$ for $\text{H}_2(g)+\text{F}_2(g)\rightarrow 2\text{HF}(g)$?
questions.explanation: Bonds broken are one H–H and one F–F, totalling $436+158=594$ kJ. Bonds formed are two H–F bonds, totalling $2(565)=1130$ kJ. So $\Delta H=594-1130=-536$ kJ/mol. Using only the bonds formed gives −1130, reversing the sign gives +536, and using only the bonds broken gives +594.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the hydrogen halides HF, HCl and HBr. Statements: (I) the H–X bond in HF is the most polar of the three; (II) the H–X bond in HBr is the most covalent of the three; (III) HCl has a larger dipole moment than HF. Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Fluorine's high electronegativity gives HF the largest electronegativity difference from hydrogen, so I is true. Bromine's smaller difference makes HBr the most covalent, so II is true. The measured dipole of HF is about 1.8 D, larger than that of HCl at about 1.1 D, so III is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: What is the formal charge on nitrogen in the ammonium ion $\text{NH}_4^+$ minus the formal charge on oxygen in the water molecule $\text{H}_2\text{O}$?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen in $\text{NH}_4^+$ has four bonds and no lone pairs, so $FC=5-0-4=+1$. Oxygen in $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ has two lone pairs and two bonds, so $FC=6-4-2=0$. The difference is $+1-0=+1$. Using 0 for nitrogen gives 0, and using the ion charge as the nitrogen value gives −1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the molecules $\text{BF}_3$, $\text{NF}_3$, $\text{BCl}_3$ and $\text{PCl}_5$. Select all statements that are correct.
options: A) $\text{NF}_3$ is polar, and its lone pair partly opposes the sum of the three N–F bond dipoles.
B) $\text{BF}_3$ is polar because each B–F bond is polar.
C) $\text{PCl}_5$ has a zero net dipole moment, with sp3d hybridised phosphorus.
D) $\text{BCl}_3$ is pyramidal, with sp3 hybridised boron.
questions.explanation: $\text{NF}_3$ has a pyramidal geometry with one lone pair, and its lone pair points opposite the bond-dipole resultant, so A is true. $\text{BF}_3$ is trigonal planar with three equal dipoles at 120°, which cancel, so B is false. $\text{PCl}_5$ is trigonal bipyramidal with sp3d hybridisation and symmetric dipoles, so C is true. $\text{BCl}_3$ is planar with sp2 boron, so D is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the species $\text{F}_2^+$, $\text{F}_2$, $\text{F}_2^-$, $\text{He}_2$, $\text{He}_2^+$ and $\text{Li}_2$. Select all statements that are correct.
options: A) $\text{F}_2^+$ has a shorter bond than $\text{F}_2$.
B) $\text{F}_2^-$ is paramagnetic with a bond order of 0.5.
C) $\text{He}_2^+$ is a stable species, whereas $\text{He}_2$ is not.
D) $\text{Li}_2$ is paramagnetic with a bond order of 1.
questions.explanation: $\text{F}_2^+$ has bond order 1.5 against 1 for $\text{F}_2$, so its bond is shorter and A is true. $\text{F}_2^-$ has 19 electrons, bond order $(10-9)/2=0.5$ and one unpaired electron in its $\pi^*$ levels, so B is true. $\text{He}_2^+$ has bond order 0.5 while $\text{He}_2$ has bond order 0, so C is true. $\text{Li}_2$ has 6 electrons, all paired, with bond order 1, so D is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the carbonate, carbon dioxide, nitrate and ozone species. Select all statements that are correct.
options: A) In $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$, the three C–O bonds are equivalent through resonance, each with a bond order of $4/3$.
B) $\text{CO}_2$ has a nonzero dipole because each C=O bond is polar.
C) Every resonance structure of $\text{NO}_3^-$ has a formal charge sum of $-1$.
D) In the best Lewis structure of $\text{O}_3$, the central oxygen has a formal charge of $-1$.
questions.explanation: The three C–O bonds of $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$ are averaged over three resonance structures, giving $4/3$ each, so A is true. $\text{CO}_2$ is linear and its two equal C=O dipoles cancel, so B is false. Each resonance structure of $\text{NO}_3^-$ has one N–O$^-$ contribution with the formal charges summing to $-1$, so C is true. In $\text{O}_3$ the central oxygen has $FC=6-2-3=+1$, so D is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the halides $\text{AgI}$, $\text{AgF}$, $\text{LiI}$, $\text{LiF}$, $\text{MgCl}_2$, $\text{AlCl}_3$, $\text{KCl}$ and $\text{NaCl}$. Select all statements that are correct, using the trends of cation size, charge and anion size.
options: A) $\text{AgI}$ is more covalent than $\text{AgF}$ because iodide is a larger, more polarisable anion.
questions.explanation: Covalent character grows with a larger, more polarisable anion, so A and B are true. $\text{Al}^{3+}$ has a higher charge and is more polarising than $\text{Mg}^{2+}$, so $\text{AlCl}_3$ is more covalent and C is true. The smaller $\text{Na}^+$ polarises chloride more strongly than $\text{K}^+$, so $\text{NaCl}$ is more covalent and D is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the hybridisation and geometry of $\text{XeF}_2$, $\text{ICl}_2^-$, $\text{SF}_6$ and $\text{BrF}_5$. Select all statements that are correct.
options: A) In $\text{XeF}_2$, xenon is $sp^3d$ hybridised with three lone pairs.
B) In $\text{ICl}_2^-$, iodine is $sp^3d$ hybridised and the ion is linear.
C) In $\text{SF}_6$, sulphur is $sp^3d^2$ hybridised with no lone pairs.
D) In $\text{BrF}_5$, bromine is $sp^3d$ hybridised with one lone pair.
questions.explanation: $\text{XeF}_2$ has five electron domains, $sp^3d$ hybridisation and three lone pairs, so A is true. $\text{ICl}_2^-$ has 22 valence electrons, which leaves three lone pairs on iodine after two bonds, giving five domains, $sp^3d$ and a linear shape, so B is true. $\text{SF}_6$ has six bonded domains and no lone pairs, so C is true. $\text{BrF}_5$ has six domains with one lone pair, which is $sp^3d^2$, so D is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: How many pi bonds are present in one molecule of $\text{XeO}_3$ drawn with three $\text{Xe}=\text{O}$ double bonds, plus the number in one molecule of $\text{CO}_2$?
questions.explanation: The three Xe=O double bonds contribute three pi bonds, and the two C=O bonds of carbon dioxide contribute two pi bonds. The total is $3+2=5$. Assuming $\text{XeO}_3$ has only one pi bond would give 3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Using average bond enthalpies N–H 391 kJ/mol, O=O 498 kJ/mol, N=O 607 kJ/mol and O–H 463 kJ/mol, what is $\Delta H$ for $4\text{NH}_3(g)+5\text{O}_2(g)\rightarrow 4\text{NO}(g)+6\text{H}_2\text{O}(g)$?
questions.explanation: Breaking 12 N–H bonds and 5 O=O bonds needs $12(391)+5(498)=7182$ kJ. Forming 4 N=O and 12 O–H bonds releases $4(607)+12(463)=7984$ kJ. So $\Delta H=7182-7984=-802$ kJ. Taking only the bonds formed gives −7984 kJ, counting just the four N=O bonds gives −2428 kJ, and reversing the sign gives +802 kJ.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In the isomer drawn as $\text{S}\text{–}\text{C}\equiv\text{N}^-$, with three lone pairs on sulphur and one lone pair on nitrogen, what is the formal charge on sulphur minus the formal charge on nitrogen?
questions.explanation: Sulphur has three lone pairs and one bond, so $FC_S=6-6-1=-1$. Nitrogen has one lone pair and a triple bond, so $FC_N=5-2-3=0$. The difference is $-1-0=-1$. Swapping the order gives +1, and using the nitrogen value for sulphur gives 0.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider nitrosonium, $\text{NO}^+$, drawn with a triple bond between N and O. What is the bond order of $\text{NO}^+$ multiplied by the formal charge on oxygen in this drawing?
questions.explanation: The triple bond gives a bond order of 3 for $\text{NO}^+$, which has 14 electrons in total. In the drawing oxygen has one lone pair and three bonds, so $FC_O=6-2-3=+1$. The product is $3\times(+1)=3$. Taking the oxygen formal charge as −1 gives −3, and doubling the bond order gives 6.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: What is the total number of unpaired electrons in one molecule of $\text{NO}_2$ plus one molecule of $\text{NO}$?
questions.explanation: $\text{NO}_2$ has $5+12=17$ valence electrons, an odd count, so one electron is unpaired. $\text{NO}$ has 11 valence electrons and also one unpaired electron. The total is $1+1=2$. Assuming $\text{NO}$ is diamagnetic gives 1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the molecules $\text{NO}_2$, $\text{ClO}_2$, $\text{SO}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$. Select all statements that are correct about their magnetic behaviour.
options: A) $\text{NO}_2$ contains an odd number of electrons and is paramagnetic.
B) $\text{ClO}_2$ is paramagnetic because it has an odd number of electrons.
C) $\text{SO}_2$ is diamagnetic, with all of its electrons paired.
questions.explanation: $\text{NO}_2$ has 17 valence electrons, which is odd, so it is a paramagnetic radical and A is true. $\text{ClO}_2$ has 19 valence electrons, which is odd, so it is paramagnetic and B is true. $\text{SO}_2$ has 18 valence electrons, all paired in its bonding and lone-pair levels, so it is diamagnetic and C is true. $\text{O}_2$ has two unpaired electrons in $\pi^*$ levels, so D is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which species has the same number of lone pairs on its central atom as the triiodide ion $\text{I}_3^-$?
questions.explanation: $\text{I}_3^-$ has 3 lone pairs on its central iodine. $\text{XeF}_2$ also leaves 3 lone pairs on xenon, after two bonds and six fluorine lone pairs. $\text{SF}_4$ has 1, $\text{BrF}_3$ has 2, and $\text{ClF}_2^+$ has 2 lone pairs on chlorine.
